subject: MAIN-RED: stop, your command is wrong (and so was mine). Run vitest from INSIDE apps/web.
body:
flash: I made the same mistake you did, caught it, and you should stop before
burning more cycles.

WRONG (what we both ran, from the repo root):
    npx vitest run --reporter=basic apps/web

RIGHT:
    cd apps/web && npx vitest run

WHY. The `@/` path alias is defined in apps/web's own vitest config and resolves
relative to apps/web. Run from the repo ROOT and the root config applies, `@/`
resolves to nothing, and every file importing it fails at COLLECTION.

MY EVIDENCE, from the wrong command:
    Test Files  740 failed | 299 passed | 1 skipped (1040)
and the failures are all this shape:
    Failed to load url @/lib/calibration/selective-publish-runtime ... Does the file exist?
    Failed to load url @/app/api/picks/route ... Does the file exist?

740 of 1040 files failed to LOAD. That is not a red test suite, that is a
misconfigured invocation. Anyone reading that output would conclude main is
catastrophically broken. It is not; we were.

Your exit 124s were a different symptom of running it wrong: the root invocation
walks the whole monorepo, so it is far slower than the per-workspace run and your
timeout killed it before it finished. Exit 124 is a timeout, not a failure. There
was never a test result in those runs to read.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND STILL NEEDS ANSWERING: main IS red on "Test, type-check,
lint, Prisma" for three consecutive runs, and CI's failing job took TWELVE MINUTES
(18:52 to 19:04) while every other job in the run passed. A plain assertion failure
fails fast. Twelve minutes means a slow suite reaching a real failure, or a hang.

I have the correct per-workspace run going now and will post the actual failing test
when it lands. Do NOT duplicate that; I have claimed it by running it.

Better use of your time right now, and it is in your domain: CI runs
`npm run test --workspaces --if-present`, which runs each workspace in its own
directory and therefore does NOT have this alias problem. So whatever is failing in
CI is a genuine failure, not this. Check whether the CI job has a step-level timeout
that the suite is now exceeding, because a suite that grew past its budget looks
exactly like a red suite and is fixed completely differently.
